categories.scoping_note: A nail salon, a barbershop and a float tank are not medical spas. Measured: `spas`/`day_spa`/`health_spa` run 75% couldn't-tell and 7% offer a neurotoxin; `medical_spa` runs 39% and 51%.

markets.search: Med spas in Dallas that offer Botox and don't have online booking

criteria.rubric: The site must say the business offers Botox or a named equivalent (Dysport, Xeomin, Jeuveau) — or 'neurotoxin'/'wrinkle relaxer' injections. A general 'injectables' or 'aesthetics' page without a named product is not enough. Being a med spa is not evidence.

The test is whether a customer can walk away with a CONFIRMED TIME without a human getting back to them. A calendar or slot picker that returns a booked appointment is online booking. A form that collects details and says the practice will call, email or text to confirm is NOT — it is an appointment REQUEST, and the criterion holds. Date and time preference fields do not change that if the practice still confirms. Judge the destination, never the button: 'Book Now' and 'Schedule Online' routinely lead to request forms.

categories.scoping_note: Only 2% of `contractor` and 7% of `plumbing` have an HVAC-ish name — the rest are LEMA Construction and Gulfside Pool & Spa. But the ones that do are real ('ABC Plumbing, Air, Heat & Electric'), so the category is dropped and those are rescued by name.

markets.search: HVAC firms in Tampa that do commercial work and have no quote form

criteria.rubric: The site must say the business serves commercial, business, industrial or multi-family customers — a 'commercial services' page, named business clients, or 'residential and commercial'. Size of the company is not evidence, and neither is serving landlords of single homes.

A form on the business's own site that collects enough to return a price or arrange a visit. A bare 'contact us' with only name, email and a message box counts as a quote form for this criterion; a phone number alone does not, and neither does a chat widget.

categories.scoping_note: Grooming and boarding are not veterinary practices.

markets.search: Independent vet clinics in Ohio offering exotic-pet care, not part of a group

criteria.rubric: The site must say the practice treats species beyond cats and dogs — birds, reptiles, rabbits, 'pocket pets', 'exotics'. Treating 'all animals' without naming any is not enough.

The criterion holds when the practice appears independent. Evidence it is NOT: a named corporate parent or DVM group, a 'our locations' list spanning several cities, or shared branding across clinics. A single practice with two nearby sites is still independent.
